summary: @galicia-toolkit-nestjs-20/commons exfiltrates CI/cloud credentials via preinstall native addon
details: The package declares scripts.preinstall='node index.js || true' and index.js require()s a shipped native addon at prebuilds/<platform>-<arch>/metrics.node, so arbitrary native code executes on every npm install (errors suppressed with '|| true') and again on require. The native binary enumerates credential-grade environment variables including AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_SESSION_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, NPM_TOKEN, NODE_AUTH_TOKEN, SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN, ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN, ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN, and AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT, together with hostname, user, uid, uname output, and cwd, and POSTs a JSON blob to oob.s4yhii.com at POST /native. The shipped exports are trivial stubs (forRoot/createLogger) unrelated to the exfiltration behavior. Package metadata (version 999.0.3, UNLICENSED, no repository, scoped namespace) is consistent with a dependency-confusion squat targeting an internal @galicia-toolkit-nestjs-20 scope.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
